sources.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite atlas for a 2D side-scrolling action game, genuinely transparent RGBA background. EXACTLY sixteen separate full-body Raiden Shogun sprites in a strict 4 columns by 4 rows grid, square canvas approximately 2048x2048. Each cell has generous transparent margins, entire curved katana, boots, braid, kimono cloth visible within its own cell with no overlap. No gridlines, text, labels, ground, shadows or environment.
References: image1 OLD raiden-actions-v3 sprite sheet is the PRIMARY pose and character reference. Image2 secondary attack and image3 portrait support costume/identity only. Faithfully reconstruct image1's row2 light attack four key poses and row3 heavy attack four key poses, expanding each to eight coherent in-between poses. Do not reinvent the attacks as straight thrusts.
Character: adult Raiden Shogun, long thick purple braid, small purple/gold flower ornament, white lilac asymmetric kimono sleeves, red obi ribbon, dark purple stockings and heels, same detailed elegant anime game art as old sprite sheet. Long curved violet katana with gold circular guard, blade length nearly torso plus thigh, never dagger or straight short sword. Anatomically natural hands grip hilt and bent elbows, each hand connected to arm; torso hips and knees rotate with sword swing. Consistent head size and anatomical scale all16, adult elegant strong silhouette. Orthographic right-facing three-quarter SIDE view exactly as old reference, eye gaze right at enemy, never frontal poster.
Reading order top row left-to-right then next row:
Frames1-8 light attack follow OLD row2: (1) left/rear hip loaded, right foot toward right, sword hand lifts hilt above forehead, blade runs overhead pointing rear-left; (2) shoulders rotate forward beginning short cut, bent elbow, blade diagonal upper-right; (3) blade sweeps across forward chest-height moving rightward, grounded slight lunge, elbow not locked; (4) blade angles DOWN-RIGHT past front waist at contact, hips follow, not a thrust; (5) blade LOW across front knees to right, crouched weight settling as OLD row2 col3; (6) elbow folds and blade returns low across body, braid follows motion; (7) straighten slightly from low crosscut into low guard; (8) old row2 col4 quiet ready stance sword low-right.
Frames9-16 heavy attack follow OLD row3: (9) wider planted stance and BOTH hands raise hilt over crown, curved blade trailing upper-left as OLD row3 col1; (10) two-handed overhead maximum loaded pose, torso coiled and hips back; (11) decisive DIAGONAL DOWN-RIGHT sword cut crossing chest toward enemy, front knee compresses; (12) sword finishes down-right toward floor, low leaning body identical to OLD row3 col2; (13) deeper forward body follow-through sword low-right identical OLD row3 col3, stable grounded feet; (14) shoulder unwinds from low cut; (15) recover legs and low hilt; (16) old row3 col4 ready pose sword low diagonal right.
Important distinct silhouettes: high-to-low ARC through light sequence; deeper bigger high-to-low ARC heavy sequence; never eight repetitions of horizontal outstretched arm. Energy only a restrained thin purple blade rim, NO broad painted effect arcs obscuring blade. Preserve pose progression and full safe margins. Real transparent background.
repairs: Edit this exact 16-sprite transparent atlas. Change ONLY spacing and framing: the image must remain exactly 4 columns x 4 rows, same sixteen characters, poses, costume, face, blade orientation and weapon design, same ordering. Uniformly scale EACH complete character including all cloth and complete curved sword to 78% of its current size, and center it horizontally in its own cell with its standing feet baseline at 88% of cell height. Preserve the SAME scaling factor for ALL sixteen sprites. This makes a generous transparent gutter around every sprite, especially long rightward sword tips in rows1-4 and overhead blade in row3. Each character and blade must stay inside its own cell, at least 20 pixels clear of each cell boundary. No clipped blades, no changes to poses, no shortening swords to fit, no text or grid lines or backgrounds. Preserve true alpha transparency.

registration: RGBA images are preserved byte-for-byte from image generation. Read-only Pillow/numpy inspection measures alpha bounds; metadata stores whole-clip standing height and individually registered foot roots. Crops do not rescale per frame. Jump tucked frames keep virtual standing root below boots so tucking does not snap the torso upward. Weapon tips are visually registered then snapped to nearby alpha-bearing blade pixels. All four attacks use arc trail and phase weights [4,4,2,2,3,3,2,2].
limitations: Pixels with alpha 1-24 are retained in native image files and are not treated as main silhouette for source-rect bounds. No image postprocessing or pixel edits were applied.
